correctness.rationale: For each ordered pair of distinct triangle sides, an affine mapping makes the endpoints independent U(0,1) and the Steiner inellipse an explicit fixed conic. The support matrix yields a necessary and sufficient segment intersection inequality. The two exact active intervals after u=tv exhaust the unit square, and the computed primitive integrates their Jacobian. The s=1 factorization yields the log 2 endpoint, expansions are derived from the explicit F(t), and the side-selection probabilities give the global formula. The checker independently verifies algebra, quadrature at 9 scales and direct geometric samples at 20 shape/scale combinations; the proof alone controls continuum quantifiers. At s=0 the hit event has zero planar measure, and at s=1 tangencies have probability zero.

originality.rationale: For the precise joint object (two independent perimeter-arclength boundary endpoints and the segment intersecting the Steiner inellipse at every homothety scale), no equivalent or stronger statement was identified. The accessible 2022 kinematic line paper integrates over motion-invariant lines, and the 2023 chord-distribution paper uses isotropic-uniform intersecting lines and records section lengths; neither computes this non-kinematic nested-ellipse hit law. Related indexed triangle perimeter-pair moments, area-floating-body results and ellipse sampling laws also do not imply the entire CDF. Originality is bounded by incomplete indexing and one abstract-only comparison.

value.rationale: A geometric probability for the canonical John ellipse and two independent perimeter endpoints has an a priori non-affine sampling law. The result isolates universal conditional geometry across all triangles, gives an exact nontrivial one-parameter elementary profile and a logarithmic tangency cusp, and derives sharp global shape extrema. The continuum profile distinguishes physical sampling conventions and is a useful exact test problem; this is more than a routine fixed parameter or table entry.
